recipes.name: Magnificent Macaroni Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon white sugar, or more to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally until cooked through but firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain.
Rinse macaroni in cold water until cool; drain.
Stir mayonnaise, onion, parsley, mustard, rice vinegar, sugar, celery seed, and salt together in a bowl.
Add macaroni and eggs and stir to coat.
Chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes before serving. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Magnificent Macaroni Salad
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for macaroni salad with egg is a classic version with sweetness from sugar and tanginess from vinegar, mixed together in a tasty blend.

video.description: Macaroni salad is a classic barbecue, potluck, or picnic side dish. This recipe is full of flavor and perfect for a party or meal prep! Pasta and hard-boiled eggs are tossed in a creamy and delicious dressing!

review.reviewBody: Best macaroni salad recipe I've tried yet! Simple but great just the way it is or a wonderful base recipe to expand on. Will be making this again with Old Bay and crab meat soon! Two suggestions: First off, more onions and a course chop or they'll get lost in it all. Secondly, it will dry out in the fridge. When it does, just add water until it gets the creaminess back! Thanks for the recipe!

Two suggestions to add to a really good recipe as it is right now. Slice some celery in addition to the celery seed - adds some much needed crunch. And to keep from drying out, thin the mayo mixture with a little milk, not water. Milk just works better and adds a subtle flavor to the dressing. My great grandmother always said if you want more flavor, add milk.

I resequenced the steps as follows: Hard-cook the eggs ahead of time (the day before, or earlier in the day). Refrigerate them until needed. When ready to begin, start slowly heating the pot of water for the elbows. Meanwhile, in a mixing bowl, stir the salt & sugar into the vinegar until they mostly dissolve. Then whisk in the mayo, mustard & celery seed. Refrigerate until needed. Prep the onion (about 2/3 cup white, sweet, red or scallions) & parsley (Italian flat-leaf). (Optional: add a rib of celery, first sliced lengthwise into 3, then finely diced. Add some chopped celery leaves, too!) Peel & dice the eggs. Stir the onion, parsley, celery & eggs into the dressing. Refrigerate the dressing again until needed. Boil the elbows until slightly (just slightly) overcooked (so they won't absorb all of the dressing, making the salad dry). Rinse them in cold water until cool; drain. Then combine the elbows & dressing. Refrigerate until cold. Stir before serving. Garnish with sprinkles of paprika (or cayenne!).

I usually Add in 1 cup of diced celery ... 1 ½ cups of shredded carrot ... 1 cup of dried cranberries or small diced Red Pepper ... ½ cup chopped cilantro ... ½ cup sweet relish and sometimes 1 cup of finely chopped walnuts! The additional crunch & color really brings out more culinary star-power as a summer side-dish!

This recipe was absolutely delicious! I followed dressing recipe exactly. I added diced green pepper, sliced cherry tomatoes, ripe olives, broccoli florets, sliced celery (in addition to the celery seed) and sliced scallions (instead of 1/3 of large onion.) I almost used white vinegar instead of rice vinegar because I didn’t have any, but went to the store and picked up the rice vinegar. The flavor of the dressing makes the dish! I will make this again and again.

Great basic recipe from which to go. I added 1/4 c of sour cream, 1/2 c water (I don't like dry salad), diced celery & sweet bell pepper, cubed cheddar cheese, ground black pepper, & some dried dill. To make it like I remember from childhood. I have no doubt that the recipe is great just as it is too. My daughter and friend stopped by and snagged a to go order of this yumminess. She stopped back today for the recipe. I also only use Helman's Mayo - it's the best.
Served with rib dinner, planning on eating leftovers the next day. There were none! Big hit, family loved it! Added finely chopped celery and used Splenda instead of sugar.

I was asked to bring Macaroni Salad to a gathering, my family doesn't usually eat mayonnaise based salads. I did half Mayonnaise and half Miracle Whips plus a 1/4 cup of ranch dressing. Also add bacon. It was a hit and I was asked for my recipe.

I must admit that the rating is anticipatory because I haven't made it yet, BUT I did read all the reviews and just wanted to add to them, my plan for this recipe. I have no doubt we will love it! The reviews have so many ideas for additions and a few ways to make it a meal on it's own. My plan is to make it and, if we can resist eating it all the first day, dividing it out and adding tuna, peas, scallions and celery for lunch one day, kidney beans, garlic, jalapenos and corn another day, and seafood shreds, a variety of bell peppers and celery another... I might try subbing plain yogurt for part of the mayo, as I think it will help it to not dry out and will reduce the fat. THANK FOR OFFERING A GREAT RECIPE AND THANKS TO YOUR REVIEWERS FOR SO MANY GREAT IDEAS! I'll post any new ones I come up with! Can't wait to try this!

Made this twice so far. Four stars as written, five with a few revisions! The second time, I used a little less seasoned rice vinegar and mustard, and a little more sugar, as it was a little too tangy the first time. Also used a little less mayo and onion the second time. I used dried parsley both times, as that’s all I had, but make sure you look up the ratio needed for dry vs. fresh. Both my husband and I love this! This recipe is a keeper!

Delicious exactly as written! This is now a regular item in my fridge. The wonderful thing about this salad is you can add other things but you certainly don’t need to. Once I added a carrot that I had on hand. Just finely diced it. I’ve used Apple cider vinegar when I didn’t have rice vinegar, and it worked great. Sometimes I use green onions instead of regular onion. One time I forgot to add the hard boiled eggs and everyone still raved about it. Great recipe!

I made this for my family without trying it out first because of the good reviews. I have made my own macaroni salad for many years and I thought I would try something new. Although my husband said it was OK, no one really liked it and I thought it had some kind of a strange taste. Very disappointing. I’m thinking maybe it just had too much mayonnaise. Definitely would never make it again.

I made this, and it was fabulous, but I made a lot of changes based on suggestions from others. I cut the mayo by 1/3. I cut the salt in half. I omitted the eggs completely. I added chopped black olives, chopped cukes, chopped celery and 1/4 tsp. paprika. I might either cut the salt in half again or omit it entirely the next time I make it to decrease its sodium content. I might add either tuna or cooked eggs to it for a complete light lunch one day.
My family loved the flavor of this and it was super easy!!

Good base recipe. I made it the first time like the directions call. It was too dry for me. I made it several different times afterwards and I decided to I mean double all the ingredients with 3 cups of pasta and it was beautiful. I also added greeny onions chat or minced I also added pepperoni to the mix, and it turned out beautiful.Everybody likes it.I love it too

I love the basic mayo sugar and vinegar dressing for all kinds of salads, and adding the mustard for egg and macaroni is perfect. I prefer more boiled egg to macaroni ratio (I just did 6 eggs to a scant 1 cup dry macaroni), and I usually cut back on the mayonnaise. I added a little minced celery this time. It’s delicious if you follow the directions to a T, but it’s a great basic recipe you can easily tweak.
My wife loves when I make this. I use two eggs instead of three.
Good basic salad. Easy prep. Didn't change anything. Will make again. Making tonight with Lemon Chicken thighs.
